summary: German physician Moritz Schreber promoted posture-correcting restraint devices and emotion-suppressing child rearing in the 1850s; Nazi doctor Johanna Haarer's Hitler-endorsed manuals taught mothers to withhold affection from infants.
keywords: The German Mother and Her First Child
Mother, Tell Me About Adolf Hitler

evidence.note: Schreber's influential posture book dated to 1855
long segment on son Daniel Paul Schreber, judge turned psychiatric memoirist
Schreber held an MD, taught at Leipzig, styled himself a child psychiatrist
Haarer born 1900 in Bodenbach (now Decin, Czech Republic); childhood segment follows
Haarer writes for the Nazi party newspaper, then her parenting book
her antisemitic Hitler children's book for young readers
works for Nazi racial policy office; praises Nuremberg laws and hereditary health
Haarer's later decline and death in 1988

notes: Two equal primary subjects, so the lifetime rule spans Schreber's birth (1808) to Haarer's death (1988). main_span runs from Schreber's 1855 book to the fall of Nazi Germany. The postwar reprints and studies of war children are covered, but only briefly, so reaches_present is false. Ruby Frank is a modern comparison only. This is part of a series that continues with Helmut Kentler.
